claim: Gain trajectories (scheduler outputs) become observable in log, trace and replay
fix: Gain trajectories become observable in the log and under replay, which recomputes them from the trace, where the `Ref` writes were invisible.
ver_evidence: probe.jl K11-045: fieldnames(Trace) = (:header, :schemas, :batches, :frames). The only batch recorded is the harness write to root input `in` (schemas ["harness" => [:in]]). src/trace.jl:1-4 and 15-19: the trace holds the checkpoint header and the drained input batches, and the log is recomputed from it by replay. A scheduler's gain output is a component output. The snapshot log holds it (src/dataplane.jl:556, every port in the signal table), and replay recomputes it, but the trace records no output.
ver_note: The doc overstates the trace's contents. The trace makes gains reproducible but does not hold them. The fix could also keep 'all three' by saying 'reproducible from the trace', so the wording is not fixed.

fix: After the run, `series` reads the retained snapshots, and the trace can re-drive a fresh `Simulation(world)` bit-identically.
ver_evidence: No TimeSeries exists in src/. src/sim.jl:2936-2956: series(sim, read_set) -> Series gathers the log's retained snapshots into columns. design/log.md:16818 (D-407) rejects FlightCore's TimeSeries in favour of this reader, landed in commit 06ed3bf8.

backing: D-269 (Position, third bullet: 'A change issued during a frame's wait lands at the next frame top, at most one budget h/p later'). That entry covers only a change issued during the wait, not one issued while a frame runs.
claim: Delay is at most one frame budget, dt_frame/p
fix: A change issued while a frame runs or waits is observed at the next frame top. While the run keeps pace, that is at most about one frame budget (`Δt_frame/p`, the frame period over the pace) later. Otherwise it is once the running frame ends ([D-269][d-269]).
ver_evidence: src/sim.jl:2100-2109: the stop word and the pause flag are read only at frame top, before the explicit yield and the pacer's wait, and run_frame! is never interrupted. A change issued while a frame computes is therefore seen only when that frame ends. With pace Inf, the default (src/control.jl:74), the budget Δt_frame/p is 0 but the delay is the frame's compute time, and a late (overrunning) frame delays it past the budget. Probe P6 (probe.jl:70-77): in a paced run with a 0.5 s budget, the time from stop! to run!'s return was 0.208 s, so the bound holds while the run keeps pace.

backing: D-027 (Position: 'explicit yield() in unpaced/pure-spin frames'), which backs the doc's narrower placement
claim: The yield is implicit in the coarse-phase sleep whenever that runs; an explicit yield() covers only the frames where it does not run (unpaced runs, pure-spin frames with budget <= margin)
fix: With devices attached, the loop yields explicitly at every frame top, before the pacer's wait, and the coarse-phase `sleep` yields again whenever that phase runs. The spin phase itself never yields ([D-027][d-027]).
ver_evidence: src/sim.jl:2107: `isempty(roster) || yield()` runs at every frame top with devices rostered, whether or not the coarse-phase sleep then runs (src/sim.jl:2108-2109, src/control.jl:186). Late frames and the frame after an anchor yield there too. Probe P5 (probe.jl:68): with margin Inf (pure spin) and one device, the ticker advanced once per frame (6 ticks), and with no device only 1 tick. No explicit yield is made when no device is attached.

claim: Init-bracket code block reads `init!(entry.device)`; the roster entry's field is `dev`.
fix: `        init!(entry.dev)` in the init-bracket block (and `entry.dev` wherever else the block names the device).
ver_evidence: src/roster.jl:255 the field is `dev::AbstractDevice`; src/sim.jl:1841 calls `init!(entry.dev)`. git log -S'entry.device' -- src is empty, so no rename is recorded.

claim: Block releases with bare `shutdown!(entry.device)`; the bracket calls the guarded `_shutdown!(entry)`, which warns on a throw and forwards an interrupt to the stop word.
fix: `        _shutdown!(entry)                 # release, unconditionally (§11.6): a throw is warned, an interrupt sets the :interrupt stop`, with a sentence after the block saying that a throw out of `shutdown!` is warned and the bracket continues, and an interrupt cutting it is forwarded to the stop word.
ver_evidence: src/sim.jl:1843 calls `_shutdown!(entry)`; src/devices.jl:619-631 wraps `shutdown!(entry.dev)` in a try that warns on a throw and forwards an InterruptException through `_request_stop!(…, :interrupt)`. probe.jl:112-113: a device whose init! and shutdown! both throw gave log [:init, :shutdown], 3 frames, lifecycle stopped, and the warning "shutdown! of device 1 (BadBoth) threw; its resources may leak (§11.6)". In the spec's block a throwing shutdown! would escape the catch and skip pop! and the report; the spec states the warn-and-continue rule nowhere.

claim: Block sets the interrupt stop with `stop!(control, :interrupt)`; no such method exists. `stop!` takes a `Simulation` or a `DeviceHandle`.
fix: `            _request_stop!(control, :interrupt)   # the stop word, issuer :interrupt; an earlier issuer keeps it`
ver_evidence: probe.jl:138: methods(stop!) are only stop!(::DeviceHandle) and stop!(::Simulation) (src/devices.jl:253, src/sim.jl:2328); the bracket calls `_request_stop!(entry.handle.control, :interrupt)` (src/sim.jl:1846). git log -S'stop!(control, :interrupt)' finds only design records, no src change.

claim: The loop masks delivery using Julia's `disable_sigint`; the code calls `Base.sigatomic_begin()` and `Base.sigatomic_end()` directly and never `disable_sigint`.
fix: The loop masks delivery across the boundary macro-sequence with Julia's sigatomic counter, `Base.sigatomic_begin` and `Base.sigatomic_end` (the primitive under `disable_sigint`), an increment that is negligible per frame.
ver_evidence: src/sim.jl:1653-1656, 2110, 2131, 2134, 1743, 1773 call Base.sigatomic_begin()/sigatomic_end() directly; probe.jl:137 found no disable_sigint in src/sim.jl, and git log -S'disable_sigint' -- src test is empty. The split ends matter: sim.jl:2131 unmasks inside the catch so a pending raise lands in the outer arm, which a disable_sigint do-block cannot express.

claim: outside a frame the forced throw is a stop like a deferred one
fix: Make the masked bookkeeping in `_run_body!` and `step!` resumable: on an InterruptException, a retrying `try` reruns the remaining steps (stopped flag, sweep, record, running = false) before the raise propagates, so a forced throw there still leaves the simulation terminal. Failing that, the doc reads: "Landing between the mask's start and the frame's `try`, the forced throw is a stop like a deferred one. Landing in the tail's bookkeeping, it propagates out of the call raw and can cut the bookkeeping short."
ver_evidence: The first window conforms: a raw InterruptException landing between sim.jl:2110 and frame.jl:87 leaves _advance! raw (sim.jl:2123-2139) and _run_body!'s arm records ControlRequestedStop (sim.jl:1693-1697). The second does not: the tail's bookkeeping in src/sim.jl:1743-1773 (and step!'s at 2286-2300) is a bare masked finally with no try, so a forced throw, which Julia raises inside the mask, cuts it short. Landing before 1772 it leaves control.running true, and lifecycle (sim.jl:512) reads :running with no record written, not a stop. A deferred raise waits for 1773 and leaves the simulation terminal. Nothing in D-268, D-398 or D-441 covers a forced throw in the bookkeeping, and D-268's Rejected list names a lifecycle stuck at running as the outcome to prevent.

claim: step! returns the requested count in the ordinary case, and fewer when the run terminated inside the call
fix: That is the requested count in the ordinary case, and fewer when the run terminated before the call's last frame, the stopping frame counted. A stop inside the last frame requested returns the full count, so a harness reads `lifecycle` to detect the stop.
ver_evidence: src/sim.jl:2107-2108 checks t_end before the frame budget, so a stop in the last requested frame returns the full count. Probe P44: step!(frames=3, t_end=0.3) returns 3 with the simulation stopped. Probe P46: t_end=0.2 returns 2
ver_note: Commit 401b858e records the change, following the 2026-11-05 docstring audit (ledger A8, sim.jl:2115 row). It corrected the step! docstring to 'A stop inside the last frame requested returns the full count, so read lifecycle to detect a stop' and left the spec alone. The fix also has to replace the next spec sentence, 'That return is how a harness detects the truncation without inspecting the clock'. A replay end also returns fewer frames without any termination (sim.jl:2264). So the wording goes beyond this one claim.

claim: From stopped, nothing advances until init!, restore! or replay! opens a new run
fix: From `stopped`, nothing advances until `init!`, `overlay!`, `restore!` or `replay!` opens a new run, and `errored` is terminal ([D-218][d-218], [D-219][d-219]).
ver_evidence: src/sim.jl:966-974 overlay! is legal from stopped and opens a fresh run. Probe P57/P58: after overlay! on a stopped simulation, lifecycle is initialized and step!(frames=2) advances 2
ver_note: D-429 (commit 4f922f7f) added overlay! as a fourth door after this sentence was written. The sentence just before it in the spec was updated to name overlay!, and this one was not.

claim: The replay drain 'does not swap the staging cells of the roster'.
fix: It takes the [staging cells](#g-staging-cell) of the [roster](#g-roster) (the list of attached device entries) and discards what they hold, applying none of it.
ver_evidence: src/sim.jl:2709-2714 and 2757: at each replay frame top, _replay_drain! calls _discard_staged! on every roster entry and on the harness, and that does `@atomicswap writer.cell.pending = nothing` and reports ReplayDiscardedStaging. Probe P001 shows a harness batch pending before a replayed frame top and empty after it, with the discard reported at frame 3 and ref left at 2.0, not 99.0.
ver_note: D-218's position records 'live staging taken and discarded (ReplayDiscardedStaging)', and the same section later says a staged batch is discarded. The sentence keeps D-101's older 'never drained' reading. Read literally, 'does not swap' is false, because the replay drain does swap each cell to empty.

claim: Failures report the offending name plus the list-in-hand
fix: The checks are attach-style. A face-name failure reports [did-you-mean](#g-did-you-mean), the offending name plus the list-in-hand it should have matched, and a checkpoint mismatch reports the recorded value beside the target's.
ver_evidence: src/diagnostics.jl:2630-2665: the CheckpointMismatch messages report the recorded value beside the target's (deployment parameters, store layout, clock, frame), not an offending name plus a list-in-hand. src/diagnostics.jl:2697-2701: ReplayUnknownFace's positional arm reports a bare position and no list. Only ReplaySchemaMismatch (2683-2688) and ReplayUnknownFace's named arm print the target's root-input list as the list-in-hand.
ver_note: D-217 ratifies ReplayUnknownFace carrying a bare position where the schema has no name, which covers part of the gap. No log entry backs did-you-mean for CheckpointMismatch. The fix could be worded several ways, and Appendix C's kind rows may need to agree.
